ideas.title: Telltales: trim the land yacht by the threads on its sail
ideas.critique: This breaks the long run of unattended devices filmed from a fixed camera: the player steers by reading threads that ride the solved flow, and the luffing comes out of the flow, not from a curve. The weak spots are a 2D solve standing in for a 3D sail, refreshed only a few times a second, which can make it feel laggy or quantised in the hands. If the trim responds slowly, the skill it promises disappears.

ideas.title: Hike out! The friends are the ballast when a gust heels the cart
ideas.critique: Real crew masses that shift and slide, and a capsize that comes out of moments rather than a script, give the game a timing challenge that is funny to fail. It depends on a sailing cart that does not exist yet, and friends that are only point masses dragged across the deck would make it read as a toy.

ideas.title: Beat to the far cairn before dusk: a sailing course upwind
ideas.critique: A race against the clock with a board of best times is the most expected wrapper there is. The strong part is that tacking has to emerge from apparent wind and wheel grip, but until the sail itself works this is a scoreboard on top of nothing.

ideas.title: The rigging sings: the stays hum the wind's speed
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Sound from physics as a way to sense the wind is fresh, and a rope that whistles before the gust arrives is a moment people would notice. But a Strouhal formula feeding string modes is a closed-form rig, not a solved flow, and listening gives the player little to do.

ideas.title: Brake down the dune: the motor runs backwards and the copper comes back
ideas.critique: The close traced film of the pot charging is the same simulated-device-left-alone shot the island has posted again and again, and the cart it brakes does not exist yet. Reversible pot chemistry driven by the motor's own back-EMF is a sound piece of the road, but it is a step to build, not a post.

ideas.title: Heave: rock the stuck cart out of its rut
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Pushes in rhythm that add up like a swing against ruts the cart dug itself is a good cooperative mechanic, and it is close to the big goal's final moment. It falls apart if the friends' bodies do not visibly lean, brace and slip; pushers that only apply a force would make it a puppet scene.

ideas.title: Sand fences raise the cart's ramp on the dune
ideas.critique: A solved 3D wind and saltation building drifts the player has shaped is real terrain physics that more can be built on, and slat fences versus board fences giving different heaps is an outcome you can discover. A time-lapse you wait an hour for is mostly something to watch, and the payoff only counts once a cart has to climb the result.

ideas.title: Forming the lead plates: a battery that grows with use
ideas.critique: This is one more electrochemical device on a bench that changes colour while you watch: the exact form of the last several posts. Capacity that deepens cycle by cycle is a nice daily rhythm and needed for the road, but it will read as Six clay pots with lead.

ideas.title: Carve a wing sail and test it in the wind
ideas.critique: Free-form shapes judged by the solved flow is the strong part: what nobody planned works or fails by what it is. The test itself (shape variants that pull or do not) repeats the paper darts' payoff, and the drawknife carving needs real hand animation not to look like a slider.

ideas.title: Race the tide on the hard wet sand
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A strip of firm ground that narrows with the real tide gives the player a time pressure that comes from the world, and crisp tracks against crumbly ones are a good thing to see. The mapping from moisture to Bekker parameters will be a fitted rig, and it needs a cart worth racing first.
